user_story: As a user, I want the app to load with dark mode and proper routing so that I can navigate between all simulation experiences seamlessly.
expected_behavior: The App component wraps everything in a dark-themed div, sets up QueryClientProvider, TooltipProvider, Toaster, Sonner toasts, PreviewModeBanner, and BrowserRouter. Routes: '/' → Index (ant colony), '/comparison' → SimulationComparison, '/tumor' → TumorSimulation, '/tumor-hunt' → TumorHunt, '*' → NotFound catch-all.
inputs: URL path in browser address bar
outputs: Rendered page component matching the route

user_story: As a user viewing the public preview deployment, I want to see a banner indicating I'm in preview mode so that I know backend execution is disabled.
expected_behavior: When IS_PREVIEW_MODE is true (VITE_FRONTEND_MODE === 'preview'), a yellow banner appears at the top displaying: 'Antelligence preview mode', explanation that frontend is for monitoring only, badges for proof system (SP1+Groth16), chain (Local), host, build label, and git SHA. When not in preview mode, returns null.
inputs: Environment variables VITE_FRONTEND_MODE, VITE_PREVIEW_HOSTNAME, VITE_BUILD_LABEL, VITE_GIT_SHA
outputs: Amber-colored banner with build info badges

user_story: As a new user, I want a landing page with navigation buttons so that I can choose which simulation experience to enter.
expected_behavior: Index page initially shows IntroPage with a full-screen background image. Displays 'Antelligence' title in large font. Three buttons: 'Ant Colony Simulation' (navigates to colony sim), 'Tumor Nanobot Simulation' (navigates to /tumor), '🧬 Tumor Hunt v2' (navigates to /tumor-hunt). A scroll indicator at bottom invites scrolling. Below the fold, an information section explains swarm intelligence with two cards (Ant Colony and Tumor Nanobot) and three common principles (Decentralized Control, Local Interactions, Emergent Behavior).
inputs: Button clicks or Enter key press
outputs: Navigation to selected simulation page or enters ant colony simulation

feature_name: Intro Page - Enter Ant Colony Simulation
user_story: As a user, I want to click a button or press Enter to enter the ant colony simulation so that I can start configuring and running simulations.
expected_behavior: Clicking 'Ant Colony Simulation' button calls handleEnter which sets isVisible=false (shows loading overlay with spinning ant), then after 500ms calls onEnter() which sets showIntro=false in Index, revealing the full simulation interface. Pressing Enter key also triggers this.
outputs: Transition from intro page to ant colony simulation dashboard

feature_name: Intro Page - Navigate to Tumor Nanobot Simulation
user_story: As a researcher, I want to navigate directly to the tumor nanobot simulation from the intro page so that I can explore medical nanobot scenarios.
expected_behavior: Clicking 'Tumor Nanobot Simulation' button calls handleTumorSimulation which navigates to '/tumor' route.

feature_name: Intro Page - Navigate to Tumor Hunt v2
user_story: As a researcher, I want to navigate to the Tumor Hunt v2 simulation from the intro page so that I can explore dynamic wave-based tumor cell hunting.
expected_behavior: Clicking '🧬 Tumor Hunt v2' button calls handleTumorHunt which navigates to '/tumor-hunt' route.

user_story: As a user, I want to configure the grid dimensions, food count, and colony size so that I can customize the simulation environment.
expected_behavior: In the SimulationSidebar, the 'Habitat Parameters' collapsible section contains four sliders: Territory Width (10-50, step 1), Territory Height (10-50, step 1), Food Resources (5-100, step 5), Colony Size / n_ants (1-20, step 1). Each slider shows the current value next to its label and updates the config state on change.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Habitat Parameters section
inputs: Slider adjustments for grid_width, grid_height, n_food, n_ants
outputs: Updated config values reflected in sidebar labels

user_story: As a user, I want to select the agent type, AI model, and prompt style so that I can control how ants make decisions.
expected_behavior: In the 'Agent Configuration' collapsible section: Agent Type dropdown (LLM-Powered or Rule-Based), AI Model dropdown (10 options: GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.1 405B, Llama 3.1 70B, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Mistral Small, Mistral Large, DeepSeek Chat), Prompt Style dropdown (Adaptive, Structured, Autonomous). All update config on selection.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Agent Configuration section
inputs: Dropdown selections for agent_type, selected_model, prompt_style

user_story: As a user, I want to enable/disable the Queen ant and choose between heuristic or LLM-powered queen so that I can test coordination oversight.
expected_behavior: In the 'Queen Configuration' collapsible section: 'Enable Queen' switch toggles use_queen. When enabled, a second 'LLM Queen' switch appears to toggle use_llm_queen. Default: use_queen=true, use_llm_queen=false.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Queen Configuration section
inputs: Switch toggles for use_queen and use_llm_queen

user_story: As a user, I want to enable predators and configure their behavior so that I can add evolutionary pressure to the ant colony.
expected_behavior: In the 'Predator Settings' collapsible section: 'Enable Predators' switch toggles enable_predators. When enabled, shows: Number of Predators slider (1-10, step 1), Predator Agent Type dropdown (LLM-Powered, Rule-Based, Hybrid), Fear Pheromone Intensity slider (1.0-10.0, step 0.5) with description text. Also displays a behavior info box explaining predator actions. The predatorDecisionCopy text dynamically updates based on predator_type.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Predator Settings section
inputs: Switch for enable_predators, slider for n_predators, dropdown for predator_type, slider for fear_deposit
outputs: Updated config values and dynamic behavior description

user_story: As a user, I want to enable/disable blockchain transaction logging so that I can control whether food collection and ant movements are logged on-chain.
expected_behavior: In the 'Blockchain Integration' collapsible section: 'Enable Transaction Logging' switch toggles blockchain_enabled. An info box describes features: log food collection events, record ant movements, immutable transaction history, smart contract integration. Default: disabled.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Blockchain Integration section

user_story: As a user, I want to set the maximum number of simulation steps so that I can control simulation duration.
expected_behavior: A standalone slider for Max Steps (10-1000, step 10) is displayed below all collapsible sections, showing the current value.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar → Max Steps slider

user_story: As a user, I want to click a button to run the simulation so that I can see ants foraging in real-time.
expected_behavior: Two run buttons exist: one in the sidebar footer and one in the legend area (visible only when no results yet). Both call runSimulation which: checks IS_PREVIEW_MODE (shows toast if preview), sets isLoading=true, starts a progress interval (increments 1.5% every 150ms up to 85%), POSTs config to {API_BASE_URL}/simulation/run with n_predators set to 0 if disabled, on success clears interval, sets progress to 100, stores results, resets to step 0, saves to simulation history via saveSimulationResult, after 800ms shows success toast. On error, shows error toast with detail message. Button shows 'Running...' with spinning ant when loading, 'Run Simulation' with rocket emoji when idle.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationSidebar run button OR legend area 'Start Foraging' button
outputs: Simulation results loaded for playback, toast notifications, loading overlay

user_story: As a user, I want to see a loading animation while the simulation runs so that I know the system is working.
expected_behavior: SimulationLoading overlay shows when isLoading=true. Displays: spinning ant emoji animation, orbiting ant emojis, pulsing queen emoji, a progress bar with shimmer effect, step messages that change based on progress percentage (Constructing colony → Initializing AI agents → Placing food → Setting up blockchain → Running simulation steps → Finalizing results), progress text showing 'Step X/Y done' or percentage, and a fun fact about ants.
entry_point: Index and TumorSimulation pages when isLoading=true
outputs: Full-screen modal overlay with animated progress

user_story: As a user, I want to see a visual grid showing ants, food, nest, predators, and pheromone/efficiency overlays so that I can observe the simulation in real-time.
expected_behavior: SimulationGrid renders a grid sized gridWidth×gridHeight with sandy texture background and grid lines. Renders: nest (🏠 emoji at center unless queen is there), food piles (🧊 emojis), ants (🐜 for workers, 👸 for queen) with color coding (gold for queen, orange for carrying food, blue for LLM, green for rule-based), predators (🦗 for LLM, 🐺 for rule-based, with 💤 if low energy). Pheromone overlays for trail (green), alarm (red), recruitment (blue), fear (orange) with intensity-based gradients and glow effects. Efficiency overlay with yellow→orange→red heatmap. Hotspot indicators with pulsing animation. Tooltips on hover for ants (ID, type, position, carrying food, steps since food) and predators (ID, type, position, energy, ants caught, hunt cooldown).
inputs: gridWidth, gridHeight, ants, food, nestPosition, predators, efficiencyData, pheromoneData from current step data
outputs: Visual grid with positioned emoji elements, overlays, and hover tooltips

user_story: As a user, I want to toggle the efficiency heatmap overlay on the grid so that I can focus on or hide foraging efficiency data.
expected_behavior: When simulation results exist, a button labeled '🔥 Efficiency Overlay' appears in the grid card header. Clicking toggles showEfficiency state. When active (default true), the efficiency overlay renders on the grid showing heatmap colors. Button variant changes between 'default' (active) and 'outline' (inactive).
outputs: Efficiency heatmap overlay shown/hidden on grid

user_story: As a user, I want to toggle pheromone visualization on the grid so that I can see or hide chemical communication trails.
expected_behavior: When simulation results exist, a button labeled '🧪 Show/Hide Pheromone Maps' appears. Clicking toggles showPheromones state (default true). When active, renders trail (green), alarm (red), recruitment (blue), and fear (orange) pheromone overlays on the grid. Button label changes between 'Hide' and 'Show' based on state.
outputs: Pheromone overlay maps shown/hidden on grid

user_story: As a user, I want to see which agent type is currently selected so that I know what kind of agents are running.
expected_behavior: When simulation results exist, a badge in the grid header shows the current agent_type with color coding: blue gradient for LLM-Powered, green gradient for Rule-Based, purple gradient for Hybrid.
outputs: Colored badge displaying agent type name

user_story: As a user, I want a legend explaining the visual elements so that I can interpret what I see in the simulation grid.
expected_behavior: A vertical legend card displays color-coded entries for: Ants (blue), Food (green), Queen (purple), Predators (red), Trail Pheromone (emerald), Alarm Pheromone (red), Recruitment Pheromone (blue), Fear Pheromone (amber), Efficiency (orange), Nest (gray). Each entry has hover scale animation.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → legend panel next to grid

user_story: As a user, I want to hover over an ant to see its details so that I can inspect individual agent state.
expected_behavior: Hovering over any ant emoji in the grid shows a tooltip with: ID, Type (Queen/LLM Worker/Rule-Based Worker), Position (x,y), Carrying Food (Yes/No), Steps Since Food (for workers only).

user_story: As a user, I want to hover over a predator to see its details so that I can inspect predator state and hunting activity.
expected_behavior: Hovering over any predator emoji shows tooltip with: ID, Type (LLM/Rule Predator), Position (x,y), Energy (out of 100), Ants Caught count, Hunt Cooldown value.

user_story: As a user, I want to play and pause the simulation playback so that I can watch it animate or stop at a specific step.
expected_behavior: When simulation is loaded, clicking '🐜 Start Foraging' button starts playback (sets isPlaying=true). Button changes to 'Pause' button. Clicking pause sets isPlaying=false. Playback advances currentStep by 1 every playbackSpeed milliseconds. At the end, stops playing unless loop is enabled.

user_story: As a user, I want to step through the simulation one step at a time so that I can examine specific moments in detail.
expected_behavior: Step Forward button increments currentStep by 1 (clamped to history.length-1). Step Backward button decrements currentStep by 1 (clamped to 0). Both are disabled when no simulation is loaded.

user_story: As a user, I want to reset the simulation so that I can clear results and start fresh.
expected_behavior: Clicking reset button calls handleReset which: sets isPlaying=false, clears simulationResults to null, resets currentStep to 0, clears loading state, shows a toast 'Simulation has been reset.'
outputs: All simulation state cleared, toast notification

user_story: As a user, I want to replay the simulation from the beginning so that I can watch the entire run again.
expected_behavior: Clicking replay button calls handleReplay which sets currentStep=0, isPlaying=true, and shows toast 'Replaying simulation from the beginning...'
outputs: Simulation restarts from step 0 and auto-plays

user_story: As a user, I want to jump to the start or end of the simulation so that I can quickly view the initial or final state.
expected_behavior: Go to Start button sets currentStep=0 and pauses. Go to End button sets currentStep to history.length-1 and pauses.
inputs: Click on go to start/end buttons
outputs: Current step set to 0 or last step, playback paused

user_story: As a user, I want to loop the simulation playback so that it continuously replays.
expected_behavior: A switch labeled 'Loop' toggles isLooping state. When enabled, reaching the end of playback loops back to step 0 instead of stopping. A 'Loop' badge appears in the progress area when enabled.
outputs: Playback loops or stops at end

user_story: As a user, I want to change the playback speed so that I can watch the simulation faster or slower.
expected_behavior: A dropdown select offers 4 speed options: 0.5x (600ms), 1x (300ms), 2x (150ms), 4x (75ms). Changing speed updates playbackSpeed which controls the interval between step advances.

user_story: As a user, I want to drag a timeline slider to jump to any step so that I can quickly navigate to specific points in the simulation.
expected_behavior: When simulation is loaded, a slider appears showing current step position. Dragging sets currentStep to the slider value (clamped 0 to totalSteps-1) and pauses playback. Progress text shows '🐜 X / Y 🐜'. A 'Done' badge appears when at the last step and not playing.

user_story: As a power user, I want keyboard shortcuts to control playback so that I can navigate efficiently without clicking buttons.
expected_behavior: When simulation is loaded and focus is not in an interactive control (input, textarea, select, button, slider, switch, combobox, contenteditable): Spacebar toggles play/pause, ArrowRight steps forward, ArrowLeft steps backward, Home goes to start, End goes to end, 'r' replays from beginning. A help tooltip (HelpCircle icon) shows all shortcuts.
inputs: Keyboard key presses (Space, Arrow keys, Home, End, R)

user_story: As a user, I want to return to the intro page from the simulation view so that I can choose a different simulation experience.
expected_behavior: A button with RotateCcw icon in the SimulationControls calls onBackToIntro which sets showIntro=true, returning to the IntroPage.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → SimulationControls → back to intro button

user_story: As a user, I want to see real-time metrics during playback so that I can monitor simulation progress at a glance.
expected_behavior: A horizontally scrollable row of metric cards displays: Step (current/total), Food collected, Active ants count, API calls, Queen status (Active/Inactive), Blockchain status (Active/Inactive), Efficiency percentage, Pheromone level percentage. All values update with each step.

user_story: As a user, I want to see the Queen ant's analysis report so that I can understand the queen's strategic decisions.
expected_behavior: When simulation results exist and use_queen is enabled, QueenAntReport renders. If a queen_report string exists for the current step, displays it in a pre-formatted block with timestamp and report length. If no report, shows 'No report available' message with debug info (report value state, component visibility).
outputs: Formatted report text or placeholder message

user_story: As a user, I want to see a line chart of food piles remaining over time so that I can track how food is depleted throughout the simulation.
expected_behavior: PerformanceCharts renders a LineChart with foodDepletionHistory data. X-axis is simulation step, Y-axis is food piles remaining. Shows a purple line with dots. Includes CartesianGrid, tooltip (shows step and food piles), and legend.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → PerformanceCharts → Food Depletion chart

feature_name: Food Collection by Agent Type Chart
user_story: As a user, I want to compare food collected by LLM vs rule-based agents so that I can evaluate agent efficiency.
expected_behavior: When both LLM and rule-based agents have collected food (>0), a BarChart displays food collected by each agent type. Two bars: LLM-Powered (purple) and Rule-Based (green). Includes grid, axes, tooltip, and legend. Only shown when shouldShowAgentTypeChart is true (both types have food > 0).
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → PerformanceCharts → Agent Type chart

user_story: As a user, I want to see a bar chart of maximum pheromone concentrations by type so that I can understand chemical communication intensity.
expected_behavior: When pheromoneData exists, a BarChart displays max pheromone values: Trail (green), Alarm (red), Recruitment (blue), and optionally Fear (orange). Color-coded bars with intensity tooltip.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → PerformanceCharts → Pheromone Intensity chart
outputs: Color-coded bar chart of pheromone intensities

user_story: As a user, I want to see a scatter plot of foraging hotspots so that I can identify areas of highest ant activity.
expected_behavior: When efficiencyData exists with hotspot_locations, a ScatterChart plots hotspot positions on an X-Y grid (0-20 domain). Points are orange, with tooltip showing coordinates.

user_story: As a user, I want to see a summary of system performance metrics so that I can monitor LLM API usage and pheromone activity.
expected_behavior: A card displays grid of metric tiles: Total API Calls (blue), LLM Agent Food (green), Rule Agent Food (orange), Total Food (purple). When pheromoneData exists, also shows Max Trail (cyan) and Max Alarm (red), and optionally Max Fear (orange). When efficiencyData exists, shows a summary with max efficiency score, hotspot count, and description.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → PerformanceCharts → System Performance card
outputs: Grid of colored metric tiles and efficiency summary

user_story: As a user, I want to see aggregate performance data from past simulations so that I can compare agent types over time.
expected_behavior: HistoricalPerformance reads from localStorage (key 'ant_simulation_history', max 15 entries). If empty, shows 'No simulation history yet' placeholder. When data exists: shows summary cards per agent type (Total Food, Avg/Run, Runs count, Min-Max range) with color-coded left borders, a BarChart with Total Food, Average per Run, and Number of Runs bars, and a footer noting 'Showing data from the last X of 15 maximum stored simulations'. Listens for storage changes and custom HISTORY_UPDATED_EVENT to refresh.
outputs: Summary cards and bar chart of historical performance

user_story: As a user, I want to export my simulation history as a JSON file so that I can analyze it externally or share it.
expected_behavior: A download button in HistoricalPerformance calls handleExport which reads history via exportHistoryAsJSON(), creates a Blob, and downloads as 'simulation-history-YYYY-MM-DD.json'.

user_story: As a user, I want to clear all stored simulation history so that I can start fresh tracking.
expected_behavior: A trash button in HistoricalPerformance calls handleClearHistory which shows a confirm dialog 'Are you sure you want to clear all simulation history?'. If confirmed, calls clearSimulationHistory() which removes the localStorage key, dispatches update event, and resets display.

user_story: As a user, I want to see blockchain transaction metrics so that I can monitor on-chain activity and latency.
expected_behavior: When simulationResults contains blockchain_transactions, BlockchainMetrics renders. Shows: metrics row (Avg Latency, Range min-max, Success Rate, Throughput split LLM/Rule), a LineChart of transaction latency over time (sampled to max 20 points), summary text with total/LLM/rule counts, and a scrollable list of last 10 transactions with type badge, step, truncated tx_hash, latency, and a 'View on Basescan' link to https://sepolia.basescan.org/tx/{tx_hash}. If no transactions, shows empty state.
entry_point: Route '/' → Index → BlockchainMetrics component (shown when blockchain_transactions exist)
outputs: Metrics cards, latency chart, transaction list with explorer links

user_story: As a user, I want to navigate to the comparison lab from the main page so that I can run batch comparisons.
expected_behavior: A button labeled 'Simulation Comparison Lab' with BarChart3 icon navigates to '/comparison' route. Appears in the Blockchain Analytics section header.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to run a Queen vs No-Queen comparison so that I can measure the impact of queen coordination on food collection.
expected_behavior: ComparisonPanel displays a 'Run Queen Comparison' button. Clicking calls POST {apiBaseUrl}/simulation/compare with current config (including comparison_steps=100). On success, shows: 3 summary tiles (food without queen, food with queen, improvement percentage with color coding), a BarChart comparing the two scenarios, and an analysis text section with dynamic message based on improvement magnitude (>10% significant, >0 moderate, 0 none, <0 negative) plus configuration details (agent type, ants count, food, grid, pheromone settings, queen type).
outputs: Comparison results, summary tiles, bar chart, analysis text

user_story: As a developer, I want to see technical configuration details so that I can verify simulation parameters and runtime state.
expected_behavior: When simulationResults exist, a Technical Details card shows three columns: Model Configuration (grid size, agents, model, prompt style, queen status), Pheromone Configuration (decay rate, trail/alarm/recruitment deposits, max value), Current Status (step, food remaining, API calls, food by LLM/rule ants, active config, predators if enabled, actual ant breakdown by LLM/rule/queen). Below: Blockchain Status indicator (green dot if active with transaction count, gray if inactive).

user_story: As a preview mode user, I want to see a monitoring checkpoint card so that I understand the build context.
expected_behavior: When IS_PREVIEW_MODE is true, an amber card appears at the top of the simulation content area showing: Title 'Frontend monitoring checkpoint', description about using preview to verify UI changes, and three columns: Mode (BUILD_INFO.mode), Build (BUILD_INFO.buildLabel), Chain (Local).

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Food Counts Selection
user_story: As a researcher, I want to select multiple food counts for batch comparison so that I can test how food availability affects performance.
expected_behavior: On the /comparison page, a 'Food Counts' section shows toggle buttons for values [5, 10, 15, 20, 25]. Clicking toggles inclusion in config.foodCounts array. Selected buttons use 'default' variant, unselected use 'outline'. Disabled during running.

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Ant Counts Selection
user_story: As a researcher, I want to select multiple ant counts for batch comparison so that I can test how colony size affects performance.
expected_behavior: Toggle buttons for values [5, 10, 15, 20]. Same toggle behavior as food counts. Disabled during running.

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Agent Types Selection
user_story: As a researcher, I want to select agent types for comparison so that I can compare LLM-powered vs rule-based performance.
expected_behavior: Toggle buttons for ['Rule-Based', 'LLM-Powered']. Same toggle behavior. Disabled during running.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to set the number of iterations per configuration so that I can get statistically meaningful results.
expected_behavior: A Select dropdown offering 1, 2, or 3 iterations. Updates config.iterations. Disabled during running.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to start the batch comparison so that I can collect performance data across multiple configurations.
expected_behavior: A 'Start Comparison' button (disabled when running or no valid config) runs runComparison. In preview mode, shows toast and returns. Validates at least one food count, ant count, and agent type selected. Iterates through all combinations (foodCounts × antCounts × agentTypes × iterations), POSTs each to /simulation/run, collects results (foodCollected, stepsToComplete, avgLatency from blockchain txs, successRate). Shows progress bar, current run description, and toast on completion. Total runs = foodCounts.length × antCounts.length × agentTypes.length × iterations.
outputs: Progress bar, results array, toast notifications

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Food Collection Performance Chart
user_story: As a researcher, I want to see a bar chart of food collected by configuration so that I can compare performance across setups.
expected_behavior: When results exist, a BarChart shows food collected (amber bars) per configuration label (e.g., '10F-5A-Rule-Based'). X-axis labels rotated -45°, Y-axis labeled 'Food Collected', with tooltip and legend.
entry_point: Route '/comparison' → SimulationComparison → Food Collection Performance card
outputs: Bar chart of food collected per configuration

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Efficiency Metrics Chart
user_story: As a researcher, I want to see steps to complete and blockchain latency so that I can evaluate efficiency tradeoffs.
expected_behavior: A BarChart with dual Y-axes: left for Steps (blue bars), right for Latency in ms (purple bars). X-axis shows configuration labels rotated -45°. Includes tooltip and legend.
outputs: Dual-axis bar chart of steps and latency per configuration

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Detailed Results Table
user_story: As a researcher, I want to see a detailed table of all comparison results so that I can examine exact numbers per configuration.
expected_behavior: An HTML table with columns: Config, Food, Ants, Type, Collected, Steps, Latency, Success. Agent type shown with colored badge (purple for LLM-Powered, blue for Rule-Based). Success rate shown in green. Rows have hover effect.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to export comparison results as CSV so that I can analyze them in external tools.
expected_behavior: An 'Export CSV' button with Download icon calls exportResults which generates CSV from results array (headers: Config, Food Count, Ant Count, Agent Type, Food Collected, Steps to Complete, Avg Latency, Success Rate), creates a Blob, and downloads as 'simulation-comparison-{timestamp}.csv'.

feature_name: Simulation Comparison Lab - Back to Simulation
user_story: As a user, I want to navigate back to the main simulation from the comparison lab so that I can return to the ant colony view.
expected_behavior: A 'Back to Simulation' button with ArrowLeft icon navigates to '/' route.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to configure the tumor domain size, voxel size, and tumor radius so that I can set up the physical simulation space.
expected_behavior: In TumorSimulationSidebar, 'Domain Setup' collapsible section has three number inputs: Domain Size (300-1000 µm, step 50), Voxel Size (10-50 µm, step 5), Tumor Radius (50-400 µm, step 10). All update config on change.
inputs: Number input changes for domain_size, voxel_size, tumor_radius

user_story: As a researcher, I want to configure nanobot count, agent type, and LLM model so that I can control the nanobot swarm.
expected_behavior: In 'Nanobot Configuration' collapsible: Number of Nanobots input (3-50), Agent Type dropdown (Rule-Based, LLM-Powered, Hybrid). When agent_type is not 'Rule-Based', an LLM Model dropdown appears (Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.2 3B).
inputs: Number input for n_nanobots, dropdowns for agent_type and selected_model

user_story: As a researcher, I want to enable/disable queen coordination for nanobots so that I can test centralized vs decentralized control.
expected_behavior: In 'Queen Coordination' collapsible: 'Enable Queen' switch toggles use_queen. When disabled, use_llm_queen is also set to false. When enabled, 'LLM Queen' switch appears to toggle use_llm_queen.
inputs: Switch toggles for use_queen and use_llm_queen

user_story: As a researcher, I want to configure max steps, cell density, and vessel density so that I can fine-tune the biological simulation.
expected_behavior: In 'Advanced Settings' collapsible: Max Steps input (20-500, step 10), Cell Density input (0.0001-0.01, step 0.0001), Vessel Density input (0.001-0.1, step 0.001).
inputs: Number inputs for max_steps, cell_density, vessel_density

user_story: As a researcher, I want to run the tumor nanobot simulation so that I can observe drug delivery to tumor cells.
expected_behavior: A '🚀 Run Simulation' button calls runSimulation. In preview mode, shows toast and returns. Sets isLoading=true, starts progress interval (+1 every 200ms up to 90%), POSTs config to {API_BASE_URL}/simulation/tumor/run. On success: sets results, resets to step 0, saves results+config+step to sessionStorage (with warning if too large), after 800ms shows success toast. On error: shows error toast. Button shows '🧠 Simulating...' when loading.
inputs: TumorSimulationConfig (domain_size, voxel_size, n_nanobots, tumor_radius, agent_type, selected_model, use_queen, use_llm_queen, max_steps, cell_density, vessel_density)
outputs: Simulation results loaded, loading overlay, toast notifications

user_story: As a user, I want to navigate back to the home page from the tumor simulation so that I can switch to a different simulation.
expected_behavior: A 'Back to Home' button with Home icon navigates to '/' route.
entry_point: Route '/tumor' → TumorSimulation → Back to Home button

user_story: As a researcher, I want to see the current step and simulation time so that I can track simulation progress.
expected_behavior: When results exist, a badge in the header shows 'Step X/Y' (blue) and time in minutes (green).
outputs: Blue step badge and green time badge

user_story: As a researcher, I want to control playback of the tumor simulation so that I can step through the biological processes.
expected_behavior: TumorSimulationControls provides: Go to Start (ChevronsLeft), Step Backward (SkipBack, disabled at step 0), Play/Pause button (toggles isPlaying), Step Forward (SkipForward, disabled at last step), Go to End (ChevronsRight), Reset button. Speed control buttons: 0.5x (1000ms), 1x (500ms), 2x (250ms), 4x (125ms). A timeline slider for step navigation. Metrics display: Step, Time, Killed cells, Deliveries, Drug delivered. Only shown when simulationResults exist.
outputs: Playback state changes and step navigation

feature_name: Tumor Simulation - Simple vs Detailed Mode Toggle
user_story: As a researcher, I want to switch between simple and detailed visualization modes so that I can control the level of visual information.
expected_behavior: When results exist, two buttons appear: '👤 Simple Mode' and '🔬 Detailed Mode'. Simple mode shows basic visualization. Detailed mode adds: zone labels (Necrotic Core, Hypoxic Zone, Viable Tumor), vessel labels ('O₂+Drug'), nanobot movement trails (dashed blue lines showing last 10 positions), direction indicators on nanobots, and higher opacity substrate heatmaps.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to switch between substrate visualizations (oxygen, drug, IFN-γ, TNF-α, perforin, chemokine) so that I can examine different biological signals.
expected_behavior: A 6-column Tabs component with tabs: 🫁 Oxygen, 💊 Drug, 🦠 IFN-γ, 🔥 TNF-α, ⚡ Perforin, 🧪 Chemokine. Selecting a tab sets selectedSubstrate which controls the heatmap overlay rendered on the canvas. Each tab has distinct active styling (blue, green, purple, orange, red, cyan respectively).
outputs: Selected substrate heatmap displayed on canvas

user_story: As a researcher, I want to see a canvas-based visualization of the tumor microenvironment so that I can observe nanobots, tumor cells, and vessels in real-time.
expected_behavior: TumorSimulationGrid renders a canvas with: light background, tumor boundary circle (red), necrotic core (gray tint), hypoxic zone (purple tint), viable tumor region (red tint). Blood vessels drawn as pulsing green circles with supply radius and glow. Tumor cells colored by phase (viable=red, hypoxic=purple, necrotic=gray, apoptotic=yellow), sampled to max 200 for performance. Nanobots drawn as colored circles by state (searching=gray, targeting=yellow, delivering=green, returning=blue, reloading=purple) with payload indicator and gold ring for LLM bots. Substrate heatmap overlaid with type-specific color gradients. Grid lines, scale bar (µm), and substrate legend. Nanobot trails in detailed mode.
inputs: domainSize, nanobots, tumorCells, vessels, substrateData, selectedSubstrate, tumorRadius, detailedMode

user_story: As a researcher, I want a legend explaining the tumor visualization elements so that I can interpret the canvas correctly.
expected_behavior: When results exist, a legend card displays four categories: Nanobot States (Searching, Targeting, Delivering, Returning, Reloading with color dots), Tumor Zones (Boundary, Viable, Hypoxic, Necrotic), Key Elements (Blood Vessel, Viable Cancer Cells, Hypoxic Cells, Killed Cells), Substrate Fields (Oxygen, Drug, Chemokine, Toxicity). Below: an info tip explaining nanobot behavior (start at vessels, navigate to hypoxic zones, deliver drugs, return to reload).
outputs: Four-section legend card and tip text

user_story: As a new user, I want to see guidance when no simulation has run yet so that I know how to get started.
expected_behavior: When no simulationResults, displays a centered Brain icon with pulsing animation, 'Ready to Simulate' heading, instructions to configure and run, and an info box explaining how nanobots navigate toward hypoxic tumor regions using chemotaxis and pheromone trails.
outputs: Guidance display with brain icon and instructions

feature_name: Tumor Hunt - Agent Type & Model Selection
user_story: As a researcher, I want to select the nanobot agent type and LLM model for the tumor hunt so that I can control decision-making.
expected_behavior: In TumorHunt config panel, an 'Agent Type' select dropdown offers Rule-Based, LLM-Powered, Hybrid. When agent_type is not 'Rule-Based', a 'Model' select dropdown appears with options: Llama-3.3-70B, Mistral-Large, DeepSeek. Both disabled during running.
inputs: Dropdown selections for agent_type and selected_model

user_story: As a researcher, I want to adjust hunt simulation parameters via sliders so that I can configure the wave-based tumor hunt.
expected_behavior: Seven range sliders: Nanobots (1-50, step 1), Max Steps (20-500, step 10), Initial Cells (1-50, step 1), Wave Interval (5-100, step 5), Cells per Wave (1-30, step 1), Max Waves (1-20, step 1), Kill Threshold (0.5-20, step 0.5). Each shows current value next to label. All disabled during running.
inputs: Slider adjustments for n_nanobots, max_steps, initial_cells, wave_interval, cells_per_wave, max_waves, drug_kill_threshold

user_story: As a researcher, I want to toggle pheromone overlay visibility so that I can see or hide chemical trail data on the hunt grid.
expected_behavior: A checkbox labeled 'Show Pheromone Overlay' toggles showPheromones (default true). When enabled, pheromone trail (green) and recruitment (purple) overlays are rendered on the canvas. Disabled during running.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to run the tumor hunt simulation so that I can observe nanobots hunting tumor cells in waves.
expected_behavior: A '▶ Run Hunt' button calls handleRun. In preview mode, shows wave notification and returns. Sets isRunning=true, clears results, starts progress interval (+1.5 every 200ms up to 90%), POSTs config to {API_BASE}/simulation/tumor/hunt with 300000ms timeout. On success: sets results, progress to 100, step to 0, auto-plays. On error: sets error message. Button shows 'Running... X%' when running.
inputs: HuntConfig (domain_size, n_nanobots, agent_type, selected_model, use_queen, use_llm_queen, max_steps, initial_cells, wave_interval, cells_per_wave, max_waves, drug_kill_threshold, nanobot_speed, drug_payload, drug_delivery_rate, pheromone_decay)
outputs: Simulation results, progress bar, auto-playback, toast/error messages

user_story: As a researcher, I want to see live statistics during playback so that I can monitor hunt progress.
expected_behavior: When results exist, a stats card displays current step number and a 2-column grid of 8 stats: Cells Alive (red), Cells Killed (green), Wave number (blue), Drug Delivered (purple), Efficiency (yellow), Searching nanobots (gray), Targeting nanobots (yellow), Delivering nanobots (green). Below: Final Results section showing kill rate percentage and cells killed/spawned/steps summary when playback is paused.
outputs: Grid of 8 colored stat tiles and final results

user_story: As a researcher, I want to be notified when new tumor cell waves spawn so that I can track the dynamic nature of the hunt.
expected_behavior: A useEffect compares alive cell counts between consecutive steps. If new cells appeared (alive + killed count increased), a red notification banner appears: '⚠️ Wave N arrived! New tumor cells detected.' Auto-dismisses after 3000ms.
inputs: Step transition data from results history

user_story: As a researcher, I want to see a canvas visualization of the hunt so that I can observe nanobots, cells, and pheromones in real-time.
expected_behavior: TumorHuntGrid renders a 580px canvas with dark background. Draws: pheromone trail overlay (green, scaled to /10.0), pheromone recruitment overlay (purple), reload stations at 4 corners (pulsing yellow circles with 'R' label), tumor cells (alive=red circles with drug accumulation arc, dead=small gray), nanobots as colored circles by state (searching=blue, targeting=yellow, delivering=green, returning=orange, reloading=purple) with payload dot, kill counter badge, and gold ring for LLM bots. Pulse animation runs at 50ms interval.
inputs: domainSize, nanobots, cells, pheromoneTrail, pheromoneRecruitment, showPheromones, canvasSize

user_story: As a researcher, I want to control playback of the hunt simulation so that I can step through the hunt process.
expected_behavior: When results exist, playback controls appear: ⏮ (go to start), ◀ (step back), ▶/⏸ (play/pause toggle), ▶ (step forward), ⏭ (go to end), a timeline slider (0 to totalSteps-1), and step counter 'X / Y'. Slider drag pauses playback.

user_story: As a researcher, I want a legend explaining the hunt visualization so that I can interpret the canvas.
expected_behavior: A horizontal legend at the bottom shows 8 items with colored dots: Alive Tumor Cell (red), Killed Cell (gray), Searching (blue), Targeting (yellow), Delivering (green), Returning (orange), Reloading (purple), Reload Station (yellow).

feature_name: Tumor Hunt - Back to Colony Link
user_story: As a user, I want to navigate back to the ant colony simulation from the tumor hunt so that I can switch simulations.
expected_behavior: A link labeled '← Back to Colony' with border styling navigates to '/' route.
entry_point: Route '/tumor-hunt' → TumorHunt → Back to Colony link

user_story: As a user, I want to see a 404 page when I navigate to a non-existent route so that I know the page doesn't exist and can return home.
expected_behavior: NotFound page displays '404' heading, 'Oops! Page not found' text, and a 'Return to Home' link to '/'. Logs debug message with attempted pathname. Uses useLocation to get the invalid path.
outputs: 404 error page with link to home

user_story: As a user, I want to receive toast notifications for actions and errors so that I get immediate feedback on system events.
expected_behavior: Both Toaster (shadcn) and Sonner toast providers are globally mounted in App. Toasts are triggered throughout: simulation start ('Sending configuration to backend...'), completion ('Simulation complete! Results loaded for playback.'), errors ('Failed to run simulation: ...'), reset ('Simulation has been reset.'), replay ('Replaying simulation from the beginning...'), preview mode warnings, comparison results, and history operations.
inputs: Toast function calls with type and message

user_story: As a preview mode user, I want to be prevented from running backend simulations so that I understand the public frontend is monitoring-only.
expected_behavior: All three simulation run functions (runSimulation in Index, runSimulation in TumorSimulation, handleRun in TumorHunt, runComparison in SimulationComparison) check IS_PREVIEW_MODE first. If true, they show an info toast explaining preview mode is frontend-only and return without making API calls. Messages vary: 'Preview mode is frontend-only. Local backend execution remains private.' / 'Preview mode is frontend-only. Tumor simulation stays local on the private backend.' / 'Preview mode only: Tumor Hunt backend stays local.' / 'Preview mode is frontend-only. Comparison runs stay on the local backend.'
entry_point: All simulation run functions across pages
outputs: Info toast and early return (no API call)

user_story: As a developer, I want the app to use environment-configured API URLs and build info so that deployments work across different environments.
expected_behavior: runtime.ts exports API_BASE_URL (from VITE_API_BASE_URL or default 'http://127.0.0.1:8001'), FRONTEND_MODE (from VITE_FRONTEND_MODE or 'local'), IS_PREVIEW_MODE (true when FRONTEND_MODE === 'preview'), PREVIEW_HOSTNAME, and BUILD_INFO object (mode, apiBaseUrl, previewHostname, buildLabel, gitSha). These values are consumed throughout the app for API calls, conditional rendering, and build info display.
entry_point: Imported globally across all pages and some components
inputs: Environment variables (VITE_API_BASE_URL, VITE_FRONTEND_MODE, VITE_PREVIEW_HOSTNAME, VITE_BUILD_LABEL, VITE_GIT_SHA)

user_story: As a user, I want my simulation results to be saved locally so that I can track performance over time.
expected_behavior: simulationHistory.ts manages localStorage with key 'ant_simulation_history'. saveSimulationResult creates an entry with id (timestamp+random), timestamp, agentType, foodCollected, steps, gridSize, antCount, foodPiles. Prepends to existing history, caps at 15 entries. Dispatches 'ant_simulation_history_updated' event. getAggregatedStats groups by agent type and computes totalFood, averageFood, runCount, minFood, maxFood. clearSimulationHistory removes the key. exportHistoryAsJSON returns pretty-printed JSON. Gracefully handles unavailable localStorage.
entry_point: Called from Index.tsx after successful simulation run
inputs: Simulation result data (agentType, foodCollected, steps, gridSize, antCount, foodPiles)
outputs: Persisted localStorage entry, custom event dispatch

user_story: As a researcher, I want tumor simulation data cached in session storage so that it persists across page navigation.
expected_behavior: After successful tumor simulation, results, config, and current step are saved to sessionStorage under keys 'tumorSimulationResults', 'tumorSimulationConfig', 'tumorSimulationStep'. Current step updates are also saved via useEffect. If saving fails (e.g., data too large), shows warning toast. saveTumorSessionItem wraps sessionStorage.setItem with try/catch.
entry_point: Route '/tumor' → TumorSimulation → runSimulation and step useEffect
inputs: Simulation results JSON, config, step number
outputs: SessionStorage entries, warning toast on failure

user_story: As a user, I want to see the Antelligence brand and logo so that I can identify the application.
expected_behavior: In SimulationControls header: an ant logo image (/ant-logo.jpeg) with hover scale animation and gradient overlay, 'Antelligence' title with gradient text, and 'AI-Powered Ant Colony Simulation' subtitle. In IntroPage: large 'Antelligence' title (text-8xl, black, drop-shadow). In TumorHunt: '🧬 Tumor Hunt v2' heading.
outputs: Branded header with logo and title

user_story: As a user, I want to collapse the simulation sidebar to gain more screen space for the visualization.
expected_behavior: SimulationSidebar has a collapse button (ChevronRight icon) in the header. When isCollapsed=true, renders a narrow 16px-wide bar with just an expand button. When expanded (default), shows full 320px sidebar with all config. Note: In Index.tsx, isCollapsed is always false and onToggleCollapse is a no-op, so this feature is present in the component but not wired to actually toggle in the current implementation.
outputs: Sidebar width changes (component supports it, but Index doesn't toggle)
